{{Short description|Unproven mathematical hypothesis}}
In mathematics, the '''Zeeman conjecture''' or '''Zeeman's collapsibility conjecture''' asks whether given a finite [[contractible]] 2-dimensional [[CW complex]] <math>K</math>, the space <math>K\times [0,1]</math> is [[Collapse (topology)|collapsible]]. It can nowadays be restated as the claim that for any 2-complex <math>G</math> which is homotopy equivalent to a point, some [[barycentric subdivision]] of <math>G \times [0, 1]</math> is collapsible.<ref>{{citation|title=Subdivisions, shellability, and the Zeeman conjecture|author=Adiprasito|author2=Benedetti|year=2012|arxiv=1202.6606v2 }} Corollary 3.5</ref>

The conjecture, due to [[Christopher Zeeman]], implies the [[Poincaré conjecture]] and the [[Andrews–Curtis conjecture]].
